title: Breaking-change classifier and safe rollout tooling for runtime contracts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Establish an operational policy and accompanying automation that classifies runtime changes (breaking, risky, non-breaking), enforces rollout gates for LTS and non-LTS channels, and provides tooling to generate and validate upgrade migration artifacts. The goal is to make all runtime API/behavior changes auditable, reversible, and supported by CI checks and canary automation so customers using Redwood Dedicated/Private experience predictable upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: A documented change-classification rubric that triages any code or spec change into 'breaking' | 'behavior-risk' | 'non-breaking'
Automation that inserts a 'compatibility' label on PRs and generates a human-readable compatibility note in the changelog for release candidates
CI gates that fail builds when a change marked 'breaking' lacks a migration guide and compat tests
Rollout orchestration updates that enforce canary percentage progression and automatic rollback triggers for LTS channel releases
A customer-facing migration playbook template and automated email snippet generated for high-impact changes
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Design rubric with applied examples (RPC surface, runtime flags, binary protocol, API response shape). Owners: Runtime API + Release Eng
Phase 2: Add PR linter rule that scans modified proto/json-schema/handler-signatures and suggests classification
Phase 3: CI job 'compat-check' that runs compatibility matrix tests against pinned older runtimes and model-serving clients
Phase 4: Console and release tooling: add 'compatibility' metadata to release notes and surface in Console per-customer upgrade hints
Phase 5: Integrate gating with rollout automation: require 'compat-approved' label for >10% canary on LTS channel and attach health monitors (latency error budget, 5xx rate, kv-cache hit rate)
rollout_plan: Draft rubric and get PR review from Runtime, SDKs, and PL teams (1 week)
Implement PR linter and compat-check pipeline (2 weeks)
Pilot on non-LTS minor release with opt-in canaries for internal tenants (2 weeks)
Iterate on signals and thresholds, then enable enforcement for LTS candidate releases (1 sprint)
Post-launch: quarterly audit of mis-classified changes and adjust rubric
migration_steps: For breaking RPC changes: provide server-side compatibility shim + client migration snippet (code example and rollout timeline)
For behavior-risk changes: include opt-out runtime flag with deprecation timeline and metric dashboard link
For non-breaking changes: automated changelog entry and zero-downtime rollout recommendation
Provide 'runbook' template for SREs describing rollback steps and artifact pinning for Dedicated/Private customers
risks: Overly broad 'breaking' classification causing excessive release friction
Missed compatibility checks for binary protocol changes affecting Private deployments
Insufficient telemetry on new signals leading to noisy rollbacks
Manual steps in playbook increase time-to-resolution for customer incidents
